claims.statement: At the pinned snapshot, a user may choose a Codespaces default editor in personal settings. This is a preference capability, not a mandated editor, verified setting or estate-wide policy.

Changing to a machine with different storage capacity temporarily makes the codespace unavailable and automatically stops an active instance; after completion it can restart on the new type. The 32-to-64 GB example is illustrative, not required sizing or cost authorization.

A same-storage-capacity machine change takes effect on the next restart and does not automatically stop an active codespace. The linked restart article remains a separate dependency, not reviewed by this fragment receipt.

Dev container Features combine installation code with configuration to add tools, runtimes or libraries and are designed for a broad range of base images. Design intent does not prove compatibility or safe code; linked feature listings and specifications remain separate evidence. No installation code was executed.
Features can be added to devcontainer.json through the editor or repository. A declared feature is not evidence of installation, reviewed dependencies or permission to execute installation code.

Codespaces port forwarding supports testing, debugging, protocol management and organization or public sharing. Describing public exposure is not authorization to expose a service or proof of authentication and access controls; no port was opened.
